video_info.caption: Is the new M4 OLED MacBook worth upgrading? Honest 2-week review 💻
video_info.notice: Sample demonstration dataset (12 comments) loaded for video 748192019482103948

insights.overall_reaction: Across 12 verified comments, reception is mixed with a neutral skew. Positive sentiment accounts for 16.7% according to VADER and 8.3% according to RoBERTa. Critical or negative feedback is measured at 16.7% (VADER) vs 16.7% (HF), with 66.7% neutral inquiries or statements.
insights.emotional_reactions: The leading emotional drivers detected in the commentary are joy (33.3%), followed by surprise (25.0%). Joy was triggered by compliments and trend affinity, whereas moments of surprise and mild criticism reflect unexpected elements or debate in the video.
insights.emoji_behavior: Audience engagement heavily incorporates emojis, with 7 comments (58.3%) containing visual icons. The most prevalent symbols are 🔥 (1x), 💀 (1x), 👏 (1x), 😍 (1x). Comments featuring emojis demonstrated a 14.3% positivity rate compared to 20.0% in text-only comments.  Notably, 😂 and 💀 appeared in both celebratory and playfully sarcastic contexts.
insights.model_comparison: VADER and Hugging Face RoBERTa achieved an agreement rate of 91.7% across the dataset (1 classification divergences). VADER relies on rule-based lexical intensities and punctuation boosters, whereas Hugging Face evaluates contextual subword embeddings. Divergences typically happen on colloquial Gen-Z TikTok slang ('slay', 'mid', 'valid') and rhetorical questions.
insights.notable_findings: A notable volume of surprise indicates a twist, unexpected tip, or shocking element in the video. High neutrality reflects users asking questions (e.g. asking for links, part 2, or product origins).
insights.limitations: Analysis is bounded to 12 retrieved comments. Neither lexicon models nor transformer classifiers have perfect sarcasm detection without multimodal audio/video context. Temporal trends reflect recorded comment timestamps where available.
